newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA JULY HELP-WANTED INDEX HIGHEST SINCE JANUARY.
newsitem.headline: CANADA JULY HELP-WANTED INDEX HIGHEST SINCE JANUARY.

text.p: Canada's help-wanted index, seasonally adjusted, rose three percentage points, or two percent, to 124 (1996=100) in July from 121 in June, Statistics Canada said on Thursday. It was the highest level since January 1991, an official said.

The help-wanted index monitors changes in help-wanted advertisements in 20 cities. It reflects the intent of employers in these labor markets to hire new workers. Increases in the index are usually followed by drops in the unemployment rate.

Following is the full text of Statistics Canada's release Help-wanted Index July 1997 The index that measures the number of help-wanted newspaper advertisements rose in July for the 12th consecutive month, this time by 2% to reach 124 (1996=100). Increases were recorded in 8 provinces. The index has increased by 24% since August 1996. Recent movements in the index are in line with improvements in other economic indicators.
Provincially, the index for Ontario advanced 2% to 126, its 11th increase in 12 months. The index for Quebec was unchanged at 110.
In British Columbia, the index grew 3% to 118. The index has increased in 12 of the last 13 months.

The index for the Prairie provinces gained 3% to reach 141. Alberta's index continued to lead the region with its 20th consecutive monthly increase in July (+3%) to 150. Manitoba's index increased 2% to 131 - its 12th increase in 13 months. Saskatchewan's index increased 2% to 127 - its 18th consecutive monthly rise.
In the Atlantic provinces, the index increased 1% to 118. The advance was led by New Brunswick (+4%), Newfoundland (+2%) and Nova Scotia (+1%) .
Available on CANSIM: matrix 105 (levels 8 to 10). Note:The Help-wanted Index is compiled from the number of help-wanted ads
published in 22 newspapers in 20 major metropolitan areas. The index is
a measure of companies intentions to hire new workers. These indexes have
been seasonally adjusted and smoothed to ease month-to-month comparisons.
Starting with the June 1997 release, the Help-wanted Index was reweighted
using the 1996 Census of Population estimates. The Help-wanted Index
series has been revised historically from January 1981. For added
convenience, beginning with the June 1997 release, the monthly seasonally
adjusted and trend cycle data series, along with the annual data series
for all provinces and cities, have been added to CANSIM.
